a1-01.q: How do you say 'It is one o'clock' in Spanish?
a1-01.why: One o'clock is singular, so the verb and article are singular: 'Es la una'. 'Son las…' is for two to twelve.

a1-01.q: Fill in the blank: En la casa de Lucía ___ mucho ruido.
a1-01.why: 'Hay' says that something exists in a place (there is a lot of noise). 'Está/están' tell where a known thing is, and 'es' identifies or describes; neither means 'there is'.

a1-01.q: Why does the story say 'Mamá está cansada' and not 'Mamá es cansada'?
options: Because being tired is how she feels right now, a temporary state.
Because 'es' is only for things, not people.
a1-01.why: Estar is for temporary states and feelings, like being tired this morning. Ser is used with people too (Mamá es alta), for what someone is like in general.

a1-01.q: Which sentence is correct for 'Lucía looks in the bathroom and Dad has a coffee'?
options: Lucía busco en el baño y papá tiene un café.
Lucía busca en el baño y papá tienes un café.
Lucía busca en el baño y papá tiene un café.
Lucía buscar en el baño y papá tengo un café.
a1-01.why: Each verb matches its subject: Lucía (she) → busca; papá (he) → tiene. Busco and tengo are 'I' forms, tienes is 'you', and buscar is the infinitive.

a1-01.q: Complete: —¿Qué hora es? —___ las tres de la tarde.
a1-01.why: Three is plural, so 'Son las tres'. Only one o'clock takes the singular 'Es la una'.

options: El café está en la mesa.
El café es en la mesa.
Hay el café en la mesa.
El café hay en la mesa.
a1-01.why: For where a specific, known thing (el café) is, use estar. 'Hay' introduces something new and goes without 'el/la': Hay café en la mesa.

a1-01.q: Fill in the blank: Papá ___ en la sala.
a1-01.why: Location of a person uses estar: Papá está en la sala (Dad is in the living room).

a1-01.q: Complete: Yo ___ pan y tú ___ leche.
a1-01.why: Tener is irregular: yo tengo, tú tienes, él/ella tiene.

a1-02.q: Fill in the blank: —¿Cuánto es? —___ tres soles.
a1-02.why: Prices use ser, and the verb agrees with the amount: tres soles is plural, so 'Son tres soles'. English says 'It's three soles', but Spanish does not say 'Es tres soles'. For one: 'Es un sol'.

a1-02.q: Mateo asks about grapes (plural). Which question is correct?
a1-02.why: With gustar, the thing liked is the subject. 'Las uvas' is plural, so the verb is 'gustan'; 'te' (to you) goes before the verb.

a1-02.q: How do you say 'I have no money'?
a1-02.why: Put 'no' right before the verb and use the 'yo' form: 'No tengo dinero'. 'No tiene' means 'he/she has no…'.

a1-02.q: Which sentence needs the personal 'a' in the blank?
a1-02.why: Personal 'a' goes before a specific person who receives the action: Mateo mira a su abuela. Uvas, naranjas and dinero are things, so they take no 'a'.

a1-02.q: Which sentence correctly says 'It is Saturday'?
a1-02.why: Use ser (es) for the day of the week: Es sábado / Hoy es sábado.

a1-02.q: Complete: Me ___ las naranjas, pero no me ___ el queso.
a1-02.why: The verb agrees with the thing liked: las naranjas (plural) → gustan; el queso (singular) → gusta. 'Gusto' would mean 'I please'.
The question is to 'you' (tú tienes); the answer is about 'I' (yo tengo).

a1-02.q: How do you say 'I see the boy'?
a1-02.why: The boy is a specific person, so personal 'a' is needed, and a + el always contracts to 'al'.

a1-03.topic: Telling time: son las / a las
a1-03.q: What does 'A las doce, las niñas comen juntas' tell you?
a1-03.why: 'A las + number' tells at what time something happens. 'Son las doce' would mean 'It is twelve now'.

a1-03.q: Which sentence is correct for 'She is from Chile and she is nervous today'?
options: Está de Chile y está nerviosa.
Está de Chile y es nerviosa.
Es de Chile y es nerviosa.
Es de Chile y está nerviosa.
a1-03.why: Origin uses ser (es de Chile). A feeling right now uses estar (está nerviosa). 'Es nerviosa' would mean she is a nervous person by nature.

a1-03.topic: Gustar to say what you like
a1-03.q: Camila answers about soccer. Which answer means 'I like to draw'?
a1-03.why: 'Me gusta' + infinitive = I like to… / I like …ing. With an action the verb is always singular 'gusta'.
Hunger uses tener: tengo hambre (literally 'I have hunger'). 'Hambre' is a noun, so 'very hungry' is 'mucha hambre'.

a1-03.topic: Telling time: son las / a las
a1-03.q: Complete: —¿A qué hora comen las niñas? —___ doce.
a1-03.why: '¿A qué hora…?' asks 'at what time', so the answer is 'A las doce'. 'Son las doce' answers '¿Qué hora es?'.
A feeling today uses estar: está nerviosa. Origin (de Chile, de México) and identity (es Camila) use ser.

a1-03.topic: Gustar to say what you like
a1-03.q: Ana says: 'Me gusta dibujar.' Camila likes it too. What does she say?
a1-03.why: To agree with a gustar sentence, say '¡A mí también!' (literally 'to me too'), because the liker is 'a mí', not 'yo'.

a1-03.q: How do you ask 'Are you hungry?'
a1-03.why: Spanish says 'to have hunger': ¿Tienes hambre? English 'are you…?' tempts learners to use estar or ser here.

a1-04.q: Which sentence means 'Julia wants to go to school'?
options: Julia quieres ir a la escuela.
Julia quiere ir a la escuela.
Julia quiere va a la escuela.
a1-04.why: Only the first verb changes for the subject (Julia → quiere); the second stays in the infinitive (ir). 'Quieres' is the 'you' form.

a1-04.q: Fill in the blank: Julia ___ a la tienda de su tío.
a1-04.why: 'Ir' is irregular; the 'she' form is 'va', followed by 'a' meaning 'to'. 'Vas' is 'you go'; 'ir' is the infinitive.

a1-04.q: Which sentence correctly says 'I don't have it'?
a1-04.why: 'No' comes first, then the small pronoun 'lo' (it), then the verb: Yo no lo tengo.

a1-04.q: Julia is looking for her umbrella. Complete: —¿___ mi paraguas rojo? … —Quiero el rojo ___ es mi favorito.
a1-04.why: Where a specific thing is uses estar: ¿Dónde está…? A reason is 'porque' (one word, no accent); '¿por qué?' is the question 'why?'.

a1-04.q: Complete: Tío, ¿___ tomar este paraguas azul? (Can I…?)
a1-04.why: Poder changes o → ue: puedo, puedes, puede. 'Podo' is a common learner mistake.

a1-04.q: How do you say 'Julia goes to the market'?
a1-04.why: Going to a place uses 'a', and a + el must contract to 'al': va al mercado.

a1-04.q: Make this sentence negative: 'Sara tiene paraguas.'
a1-04.why: 'No' goes directly before the verb: Sara no tiene paraguas.

a1-04.q: What does '¡Allí está el paraguas rojo!' mean?
options: There is a red umbrella over there somewhere.
The red umbrella is from there.
a1-04.why: 'Allí está + specific thing' = There it is! A new, unknown umbrella would use hay: Allí hay un paraguas rojo.

a1-05.q: Fill in the blank to say 'There are no eggs': Pero ___ huevos.
a1-05.why: 'No hay' means 'there is/are not'. 'No' always comes before hay, and hay does not change for plural.

a1-05.q: Which sentence is correct for 'Sofía and Diego want to make a cake'?
options: Sofía y Diego quieres hacer un pastel.
Sofía y Diego quiere hacer un pastel.
Sofía y Diego quieren hacen un pastel.
Sofía y Diego quieren hacer un pastel.
a1-05.why: The first verb matches 'they' (quieren) and the second stays in the infinitive (hacer).

a1-05.q: What does 'Voy a la tienda' mean?
options: I am going to the store.
He is going to the store.
a1-05.why: 'Voy' is the 'I' form of ir (to go), and 'a' means 'to' before a place. The Spanish present can mean 'I am going'.
'A las + number' says at what time something happens. 'Son las seis' means 'It is six'. Spanish never uses 'en' with clock times.

a1-05.q: What does 'En la cocina hay leche, pero no hay huevos' mean?
options: There is no milk in the kitchen, but there are eggs.
The milk is in the kitchen, but the eggs are not.
In the kitchen there is milk, but there are no eggs.
In the kitchen there is milk and eggs.
a1-05.why: 'Hay' = there is; 'no hay' = there are no. It says what exists, not where known items are (that would be 'la leche está…').

a1-05.q: Complete: Nosotros ___ huevos, leche y azúcar.
a1-05.why: Necesitar is regular; with nosotros the ending is -amos: necesitamos.

a1-05.q: Which sentence means 'I'm going to buy eggs' (a plan, not a place)?
a1-05.why: 'Voy a + infinitive' = I'm going to (do). Keep the 'a' and keep the second verb in the infinitive. 'Voy a la tienda' is about a place.
One o'clock is singular: a la una. From two on it is plural: a las dos.

a1-06.q: Which sentence means 'I get up at six'?
a1-06.why: With 'I', the pronoun is 'me' and the verb ends in -o. The pronoun goes before the verb as a separate word.

a1-06.q: Fill in the blank: Yo ___ en Valencia.
a1-06.why: With 'yo', regular verbs end in -o: vivo. 'Vive' is he/she, 'vives' is you.

a1-06.q: Which sentence correctly says 'The bus stop is on my street'?
options: La parada está en mi calle.
La parada tiene en mi calle.
La parada es en mi calle.
La parada hay en mi calle.
a1-06.why: Where a specific thing is uses estar: La parada está en mi calle. 'Hay' would need 'una': Hay una parada en mi calle.

a1-06.q: Complete: Me ___ mucho mi viaje, pero no me ___ los lunes.
a1-06.why: Gustar agrees with the thing liked: mi viaje (singular) → gusta; los lunes (plural) → gustan.

a1-06.q: Complete: Todos los días tú ___ a las siete.
a1-06.why: The pronoun matches the subject: tú → te levantas. 'Se levanta' is he/she.

a1-06.q: How do you say 'I have a book'?
a1-06.why: Tener is irregular in the yo form: tengo. 'Tiene' is he/she.

a1-06.q: Complete: Mi trabajo está muy ___ mi casa.
a1-06.why: Location words take 'de' before the place: lejos de (far from), cerca de (near).

a1-06.q: Which sentence means 'I like my bus ride a lot'?
options: Me gusta mi viaje mucho de.
a1-06.why: One thing (mi viaje) → gusta, and 'mucho' follows the verb. 'Gusto' would mean 'I please'.

a1-07.q: Fill in the blank: Ana y Tomás ___ mojados.
a1-07.why: Being wet is a temporary state, so estar; two people need the plural 'están'.

a1-07.q: Which sentence is correct for 'There is a free table'?
a1-07.why: 'Hay' introduces something that exists; it does not change. 'Está' needs a specific thing (la mesa está libre), and 'Es una mesa libre' means 'It is a free table'.

options: Ana is sitting next to her.
a1-07.why: 'Sentarse' is reflexive: she seats herself, so she sits down.

a1-07.topic: Present tense with vivir and leer
a1-07.q: Tomás asks Ana where she lives. Which question is correct?
a1-07.why: For tú, -ir verbs end in -es: vives. 'Vive' is the él/ella form and does not go with tú.

a1-07.q: Why is it 'su ropa está mojada' and not 'su ropa están mojadas'?
options: Because 'está' is used for all subjects.
Because clothes are things, not people.
a1-07.why: 'La ropa' (clothes) is a singular noun in Spanish, so the verb and adjective are singular: está mojada.
'Esta silla' is a specific chair, so use estar: ¿Está libre esta silla? 'Hay' only introduces something new.

a1-07.q: Complete: Hola, ___ Tomás. (My name is Tomás.)
a1-07.why: Llamarse is reflexive: me llamo (I am called). 'Se llama' is for he/she; 'llamo' alone means 'I call'.

a1-07.topic: Present tense with vivir and leer
a1-07.q: Complete: Ana ___ el mismo libro que Tomás.
a1-07.why: For él/ella, -er verbs end in -e: lee. Leo = I read, lees = you read.

a1-08.q: Which sentence means 'You have to come tomorrow'?
a1-08.why: 'Tener que' + infinitive = have to. Don't drop 'que', and keep the second verb in the infinitive (venir).

a1-08.q: Complete: Mis flores son más bonitas ___ las del mercado.
a1-08.why: Comparisons use 'más + adjective + que' (more … than). 'De' and 'como' are typical English-speaker mistakes here.

a1-08.q: Nico is ten. How do you say it in Spanish?
a1-08.why: Spanish uses tener for age: Nico tiene diez años, literally 'has ten years'.

a1-08.q: Complete: ¿___ estás triste? — Estoy triste ___ tengo poco dinero.
a1-08.why: '¿Por qué?' (two words, accent) asks why; 'porque' (one word) answers because.
'I have to' = tengo que + infinitive. 'Tengo regar' drops the needed 'que'.

a1-08.q: How do you say 'The roses are prettier than the flowers at the market'?
options: Las rosas son más bonitas que las flores del mercado.
Las rosas son bonitas más que las flores del mercado.
Las rosas son más bonitas de las flores del mercado.
Las rosas son más bonito que las flores del mercado.
a1-08.why: Más goes before the adjective, the adjective agrees with 'las rosas' (bonitas), and the comparison word is 'que'.
Age questions use tener too: ¿Cuántos años tienes? = How old are you?

a1-08.q: Nico answers '¿Por qué estás triste?'. Which answer is written correctly?
a1-08.why: The answer 'because' is one word with no accent: porque.

a1-09.topic: Ir a + infinitive: the near future
a1-09.q: Which sentence means 'What are you going to do on Saturday?'
a1-09.why: Ir + a + infinitive: vas a hacer. Don't drop 'a', and don't conjugate the second verb.

a1-09.q: Marta answers: 'Estoy bien, pero un poco triste.' What did Javier ask?
a1-09.why: '¿Qué tal estás?' (How are you?) asks how someone is, so 'Estoy bien' answers it. ¿Dónde? asks where; ¿Quién? asks who.

a1-09.topic: Ser for time, estar for feelings
a1-09.q: Fill in the blank: Hoy ___ viernes y yo ___ bien.
a1-09.why: Ser gives the day (es viernes), and estar gives how you feel (estoy bien).

a1-09.q: What does 'El sábado no va a estar sola' mean?
options: She was not alone on Saturday.
On Saturday she is not going to be alone.
a1-09.why: 'El' before a day means 'on' (this one Saturday; 'los sábados' would be every Saturday), and 'va a estar' is the near future.

a1-09.topic: Ir a + infinitive: the near future
a1-09.q: Complete: Mañana nosotros ___ cocinar una tortilla.
a1-09.why: Near future = ir + a + infinitive; with nosotros: vamos a cocinar.

a1-09.q: Complete: —¿___ vive tu familia? —Mi familia vive lejos.
a1-09.why: The answer 'lejos' (far away) gives a place, so the question word is ¿Dónde? (where), with an accent.

a1-09.topic: Ser for time, estar for feelings
options: Está viernes y soy en Sevilla.
Es viernes y soy en Sevilla.
Es viernes y estoy en Sevilla.
a1-09.why: Day of the week → ser (es viernes). Where you are → estar (estoy en Sevilla). 'I'm fine' is 'Estoy bien'.

a1-09.q: Complete: ___ sábado voy a comer con Marta. (On Saturday…)
a1-09.why: Spanish uses just 'el' for 'on' with days: el sábado. 'En el sábado' is a typical English-speaker mistake.

a1-10.q: Which sentence means 'On Saturday we are going to go to the beach'?
options: El sábado vamos ir a la playa.
El sábado vamos a ir a la playa.
El sábado vamos a vamos a la playa.
El sábado van a ir a la playa.
a1-10.why: 'Vamos' is 'we', then 'a' and an infinitive (ir). 'Van a' would be 'they are going to'.

a1-10.q: Complete: ___ viernes ___ noche, los hermanos preparan las mochilas.
a1-10.why: No word for 'on' before days: el viernes. Without a clock time, use 'por la noche'; 'de la noche' only follows a clock time (a las diez de la noche).

a1-10.q: Raúl asks where the tickets are. Which question is correct?
a1-10.why: Location uses estar, and plural 'los billetes' needs 'están'.

options: El mar es más grande de mi casa.
El mar es grande más que mi casa.
a1-10.why: Age uses tener (tiene ochenta años). Comparisons are 'más + adjective + que', so the other two are wrong as well.

a1-10.q: What does 'Vamos a comer pescado' mean in the story?
options: They are going to eat fish.
We are going to eat fish.
a1-10.why: Vamos a + infinitive = we are going to (do). Vamos is 'we', not 'they' (van).

a1-10.q: How do you say 'The train leaves at eight in the morning'?
options: El tren sale a las ocho de la mañana.
El tren sale en las ocho de la mañana.
El tren sale las ocho de la mañana.
El tren sale a la ocho de la mañana.
a1-10.why: Clock time = 'a las + number', and after a clock time use 'de la mañana'.
Location of known things uses estar, plural for 'los billetes': Aquí están (Here they are).

a1-10.q: Complete: El abuelo ___ ochenta años y el mar es más grande ___ el lago.
a1-10.why: Age uses tener; comparisons use 'más … que'.
